test_title: PYST 19: SSC MTS - Reasoning (Held on: 22 Oct 2021 Shift 2)
subject: reasoning
question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statement is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All ponds are lakes.

No river is a pond.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some rivers are not lakes.

II. No river is a lake.

III. Some rivers are lakes.

options.text: Either conclusion II or III follows
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

solution:
__**Least possible Venn diagram**__:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b58ab1910d4f0e35d3eb47fa4345c2c4380761f969c870ef009865f8d3fb40fa.png] 

**Conclusions**:

I. Some rivers are not lakes →** **Doesn't Follow (As all ponds are Lake and no pond is river but some rivers could be lake and lake that is pond could not be river so we can say that Some rivers are not lakes is a possibility not definite)

II. No river is a lake →** **could be possible (As all ponds are Lake and no pond is river so we can not say anything about No river is a lake. it could be possible)

This possibility scenarios can be shown using the below Venn diagram:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b58ab1910d4f0e35d3eb47fa4345c2c4380761f969c870ef009865f8d3fb40fa.png] 

III. Some rivers are lakes → **could be possible** (As all ponds are Lake and no pond is river but some rivers could be lake and lake that is pond could not be river so we can say that Some rivers are lakes is a possibility)

This possibility scenarios can be shown using the below Venn diagram:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b58ab1910d4f0e35d3eb47fa4345c2c4380761f969c870ef009865f8d3fb40fa.png] 

Thus the either-or scenario is applicable in the conclusion II and III because elements in the conclusion II and III are the same and there is a possibility shown in both conclusions.

Here, **Either conclusion II or III follow**.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

Complementary pair

1) When both the elements of conclusions are the same.

2) When both the conclusions are false individually.

There are only two different types of complementary pairs, which satisfy the condition of either or.

​1) All - Some not

2) No - Some

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**"Some + Some not" are complementary pairs of Neither nor case.
